title: SMART: Semantic Segment Mapping and Assessment of Recognition Transcripts with Contextual Rubrics
abstract: arXiv:2610.27820v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Word error rate (WER) assigns equal cost to lexical edits despite their different semantic consequences, while overall semantic scores cannot identify which individual errors alter the intended meaning. We formulate ASR semantic evaluation as context-aware, segment-level consequence assessment and propose Semantic Segment Mapping and Assessment of Recognition Transcripts with Contextual Rubrics (SMART), a framework for traceable semantic evaluation and targeted ASR correction. SMART maps reference-hypothesis discrepancies into coherent segments and applies a structured contextual rubric to assign explicit consequence labels. These labels support Semantic Impact Error Rate (SIER), which quantifies consequential errors at utterance, chunk, and lexical levels. translated_title: SMART：基于上下文评分准则的识别转写文本语义分段映射与评估
translated_abstract: 词错误率（WER）对所有词汇编辑赋予相同的代价，尽管它们造成的语义后果各不相同；而整体语义评分又无法识别出哪些具体错误改变了原本想表达的意思。我们将语音识别（ASR）的语义评估形式化为具有上下文感知能力的分段级后果评估，并提出了SMART（Semantic Segment Mapping and Assessment of Recognition Transcripts with Contextual Rubrics，基于上下文评分准则的识别转写文本语义分段映射与评估），一个用于可追溯语义评估和有针对性ASR纠错的框架。SMART将参考文本与识别文本之间的差异映射为连贯的语义片段，并应用结构化的上下文评分准则为各片段分配明确的后果标签。这些标签进一步支持语义影响错误率（SIER），可在话语、片段和词汇三个层面量化具有语义影响的错误。以人类多数投票标注为基准的评估中，SMART达到了0.843的F1分数，而直接使用大语言模型判断仅为0.745。跨多个大语言模型的评估进一步表明，SMART相对不敏感……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 提出SMART框架，将ASR识别文本与参考文本的差异映射为语义片段并利用上下文评分准则标注其语义后果，从而实现可追溯的语义评估，其提出的语义影响错误率（SIER）性能显著优于直接使用大语言模型判断。
en_tdlr: SMART maps reference-hypothesis discrepancies in ASR transcripts into semantic segments and assigns contextual consequence labels via structured rubrics, enabling traceable semantic evaluation through Semantic Impact Error Rate (SIER) that outperforms direct LLM judgment (0.843 vs. 0.745 F1).
